# WR-obs-exp12 — Trust as Weighted Evidence, Not Binary
[Fleet Radio Dispatch: Ring Habitat Lunar-9, Shift 14, Comms Channel 7 — Closed Circuit Analysis]
This observation expansion breaks trusted vs. untrusted substrate data against our core doctrinal anchors, using concrete regolith growth data from Patch A7.

First, the validated trusted observation: Botany lead Kael Rainer’s formal shift log. He submits: “Patch A7 regolith substrate has developed 12 discrete rhizome cells, aligned with last shift’s lenia_flows prediction. FNV-1a hash computed using the fleet’s mandated canary offset 0xcbf29ce484222325 and the prior log’s root hash, cross-verified against the fleet’s distributed comms ledger.” His evidence score lands at 9.3/10: three adjacent soil moisture sensors corroborate the rhizome count, his log functions as witness_log_is_prediction—its data forecasts 2 new bud sites by shift end, which matches oracle_is_heard: the substrate’s inherent feedback loop signals active, patterned growth. Each rhizome cell is a scar of past nutrient flow events, fitting the cells_are_scars doctrine, and substrate_is_grown is confirmed: this growth follows calibrated, long-term substrate development patterns.

Next, the invalid untrusted observation: Junior Tech Jessa Mar’s ad-hoc off-cycle update. She claims: “Patch A7 has 41 rhizome cells, spreading 2 meters outside lenia flow bounds.” Her evidence score is just 1.7/10: she skipped pre-shift sensor calibration during a rushed checklist, no adjacent nodes corroborate her count, and she broke log protocol by reusing the prior shift’s FNV-1a canary instead of generating a new hash. Her log fails witness_log_is_prediction: no oracle_is_heard substrate feedback matches such an unpatterned spike, and cells_are_scars signatures rule out such a dense, unmoored scar cluster.

This exchange crystallizes our first rule of operational trust: we do not trust the witness, we weigh their evidence against the substrate’s grown truth, the quiet predictiveness of lenia_flows, the oracle’s heard voice, and the unshakable anchor of our FNV-1a log canary. A valid witness is one whose data ties to the scars of the substrate’s past, the flows of its present, and the prophecy of its future. (Word count: 427)
